# xqlib-cli

Scaffolding CLI that generates a ready-to-build JavaScript library project from one command:
either a webpack-bundled UMD library or a UMD + ES-module library with committed minified builds.
Runs on Node.js >= 18 and ships as a binary only — there is no `main`, `exports`, or importable API,
so consume it through the `xqlib-cli` executable, never through `require('xqlib-cli')`.

## Install

```sh
npm install xqlib-cli -g   # global binary
npx xqlib-cli -h           # or run once without installing
```

## Commands

| Command | Effect | Exit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xqlib-cli -l, --lib <name>` | Scaffold the webpack template into `./<name>` | 0 on success |
| `xqlib-cli -u, --umd <name>` | Scaffold the UMD + ESM template into `./<name>` | 0 on success |
| `xqlib-cli -v, --version` | Print `xqlib-cli@<version>` | 0 |
| `xqlib-cli -i, --info` | Print `name:`, `version:`, `author:` lines | 0 |
| `xqlib-cli -h, --help` (or no arguments) | Print usage | 0 |
| Any invalid input | Print `Error: ...` on stderr | 1 |

## Key Rules

- `<name>` is both the created directory and the `name` field of the generated `package.json`.
  It must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$` and be at most 214 characters: lowercase letters, digits,
  `.`, `-`, `_`, starting with a letter or digit. Uppercase, spaces, a leading dot, and any path
  separator are rejected, so scaffolding never writes outside the current directory.
- `-l` and `-u` are mutually exclusive; passing both exits 1 without touching disk.
- The target directory is created relative to the current working directory. An existing path of
  the same name is refused (`The library name already exists!`), so a failed or repeated run never
  silently overwrites files.
- The scaffold writes files only; it never runs `npm install` and needs no network access.

## Generated webpack template (`-l`)

- Entry chain: `index.js` -> `lib/index.js`, bundled to `dist/mytest.js` with webpack
  (`library: 'mytest'`, `libraryTarget: 'umd'`, `jquery` kept external as global `jQuery`).
- `package.json` sets `main` to `./dist/mytest.js`; scripts are `build` (`webpack`), `pretest`
  (`webpack`) and `test` (`jest`), so `npm test` rebuilds before running jest.
- Also ships `add.test.js`, `babel.config.js`, `example/node.js`, `example/browser.html`,
  `README.md`, `zh.md`, `.gitignore`.
- Next steps: `cd <name> && npm install && npm run build && npm test`.

## Generated UMD template (`-u`)

- `package.json` sets `main` to `lib/example.js`, `module` to `lib/example-esm.js`, `unpkg` to
  `lib/example.min.js`; all four builds are committed, so publishing needs no build step.
- The library object is `{ name: 'example', add(a, b), sayHi(name) }`, exposed as global `example`
  in the browser, via CommonJS, via AMD, and as the default ES-module export.
- Scripts: `test` (`node test/node.js`, zero-dependency assertions over the readable and minified
  builds) and `test:browser` (`node test/server.js`, static server for the self-checking pages,
  default `http://localhost:4001`, overridable with `PORT` / `HOST`).
- `test/` pages cover the global, CommonJS-on-node, AMD and ES-module paths and print PASS/FAIL.
- Next steps: `cd <name> && npm test && npm run test:browser`.

## Typical Use

```sh
# Create a UMD library named "my-lib", then verify it
npx xqlib-cli -u my-lib
cd my-lib
npm test
npm run test:browser
```

```sh
# Create a webpack-bundled library and build it
npx xqlib-cli -l my-lib
cd my-lib
npm install
npm run build
```

```sh
# Script-safe: the exit code is authoritative
npx xqlib-cli -u my-lib || echo "scaffold failed"
```

## Constraints

- Node.js >= 18; the only runtime dependency is `commander`.
- Names are case-sensitive and must be lowercase; the generated project keeps the name verbatim.
- The ES-module test page must be served over HTTP — `type="module"` is blocked on `file://`.
- The webpack template's demo page expects jQuery to be loaded by the page itself, because
  `jquery` is declared external in `webpack.config.js`.
- Generated projects are ordinary npm packages: `xqlib-cli` is not a runtime dependency of them.
